This exclusion does not apply to: (a) Losses falling within Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap); (b) Losses covered by an express indemnity in this Agreement; (c) breach of confidentiality, data-protection or information-security obligations; or (d) Losses arising from misuse of Customer Assets.
40.buyside: Preserved Direct Losses (Buy-Side). For the purposes of this Clause, the following are agreed to be recoverable direct losses and are not excluded as indirect or consequential loss: (a) the costs of data remediation and forensic investigation; (b) regulatory fines, penalties and enforcement costs attributable to the Counterparty's breach, to the extent recoverable at law; (c) the costs of procuring replacement services; (d) customer compensation or refunds caused by the Counterparty's breach; and (e) the cost of business interruption directly caused by a Service Level failure of the Counterparty.
40.sellside: Company Excluded Losses. Subject to Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap), the Company shall not be liable for: (a) loss of profit, revenue, anticipated savings, trading income, investment performance or business opportunity; (b) loss of data, Digital Assets or account balances arising from customer error, market conditions or third-party service failures; (c) business interruption caused by exchange outages, blockchain-network congestion, settlement-system failure or force majeure; or (d) indirect or derivative loss of any kind, howsoever arising.
40.counselNotes: Accept a mutual consequential-loss exclusion only where direct losses are preserved for all key breach categories and remedies for data breach, Security Incident, IP infringement and regulatory breach are not removed.

41.title: Insurance
41.sellside: Company Insurance. The Company makes no warranty that it maintains any specific level of insurance, and the existence of any Company insurance does not expand the Company's liability under this Agreement. The Counterparty is responsible for maintaining its own insurance appropriate to its obligations.
41.fallback: Reduced Insurance (Low-Risk). For low-risk, lower-value contracts, the Counterparty shall maintain insurance at commercially reasonable levels, including cyber and professional-indemnity cover, without being required to name the Company as additional insured.
41.counselNotes: The reduced insurance position is acceptable only for low-risk, lower-value contracts; for regulated, data-intensive or higher-value contracts apply the Baseline cover and Buy-Side terms.

42.title: Audit, Inspection, Records and Regulatory Access
42.baseline:
Audit, Inspection, Records and Regulatory Access. The Counterparty shall:
(a) keep complete, accurate and up-to-date records relating to its obligations under this Agreement, including financial, service, data-processing, security, personnel and compliance records;
(b) retain those records for at least [seven (7)] years after termination; and
(c) permit the Company, its authorised auditors and any Regulator to audit, inspect and verify compliance with this Agreement and Applicable Law on [thirty (30)] days' written notice, or immediately in the event of a Security Incident, suspected breach or Regulator request.
42.sellside: Company-Side Audit Limits. Where the Company is the supplier, audit rights are limited to: (a) verification of the Counterparty's compliance with the usage restrictions, licence scope, data obligations and security requirements; (b) an annual frequency on [thirty (30)] days' notice; and (c) confidentiality obligations protecting the Company's other customers' data.
42.fallback: Assurance-Report Audit (Low-Risk). For standard SaaS and low-risk contracts, an annual SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) report is accepted in lieu of a direct audit, and a direct audit right arises only on a Security Incident, suspected breach or Regulator request.
42.counselNotes: Accept the assurance-report approach only for standard SaaS / low-risk contracts; retain full audit and Regulator-access rights for regulated, critical or data-intensive services.

43.title: Reporting Obligations
43.baseline: Reporting Obligations. The Counterparty shall provide the Company with reports at the frequency and in the format specified in Schedule [●] (Reporting), including: (a) monthly SLA and KPI performance reports; (b) incident and security reports within the timelines in Clause [●] (Security Incident and Data Breach Notification); (c) reconciliation reports for Customer Assets or financial flows; (d) compliance and regulatory-status reports; and (e) subcontractor lists and changes.
43.buyside: Enhanced Reporting. For regulated, customer-facing or critical services, the Counterparty shall also provide: (a) real-time alerts and dashboards for critical operational events; (b) a root-cause analysis within [five (5)] Business Days of any material incident; (c) regulatory and compliance certifications on a [quarterly / annual] basis; and (d) immediate reporting of any material adverse change affecting its ability to perform.
43.sellside: Company Reporting. The Company's reporting is limited to what is expressly agreed in the applicable Service Levels or Schedule. No reporting obligation requires the Company to disclose information that is commercially sensitive, legally privileged or confidential to its other customers.
43.fallback: Quarterly Reporting (Lower-Risk). For non-critical, lower-risk engagements, reporting may be provided quarterly, provided that incident reporting, material compliance-breach reporting and material-change notification are provided as and when they arise.
43.counselNotes: Quarterly reporting is acceptable for non-critical engagements, but incident, material-compliance-breach and material-change reporting must always be provided promptly.

44.title: Change Control
44.baseline: Change Control. No change to the Services, the Fees, the Service Levels, data flows, security architecture, subcontractors, regulatory responsibilities, integration design, operational dependencies or any other material obligation is binding unless agreed in a written change order signed by authorised representatives of both Parties. The Company may reject any proposed change, and the Counterparty shall not implement any change that has not been approved in writing.
44.buyside: Change-Order Requirements. Each change-order request shall set out: (a) a description of the proposed change and its impact on the Services, the Fees, timelines and the Service Levels; (b) its impact on data flows, security, compliance and regulatory obligations; (c) the Company's engineering and security review where the change is technically material; and (d) Legal review and approval before signature.
44.sellside: Company Platform Changes. The Company may make non-material changes to the Platform (including updates, bug fixes and security patches) without the Counterparty's consent, provided they do not materially degrade the core functionality of the Services. The Company shall give the Counterparty [thirty (30)] days' advance notice of any material platform change.
44.fallback: Operational Change Notices. Operational change notices (without a formal change order) are permitted only for: (a) administrative changes (such as contact details or notice addresses); and (b) minor technical updates with no legal, commercial or security impact.

45.title: Suspension Rights
45.baseline: Suspension Rights. The Company may immediately suspend access, performance, payment of Fees or any affected Services, without prior notice and without liability, where it determines that suspension is necessary to prevent or mitigate: (a) a Security Incident or data-breach risk; (b) a breach of Applicable Law or Regulatory Requirements; (c) an AML/CFT, sanctions or financial-crime risk; (d) a risk to Customer Assets; (e) fraud or suspected fraud; or (f) a material risk to the Company's operational integrity, reputation or regulatory standing. The Company shall notify the Counterparty of the suspension as soon as reasonably practicable and shall lift it once the risk has been remediated.
45.buyside: No Liability for Good-Faith Suspension. The Company shall not be liable for any loss, cost, damage or claim arising from a suspension made in good faith. The right to suspend is in addition to, and does not limit, any other right or remedy available to the Company.
45.sellside: Company Suspension (Counterparty Use). The Company may immediately suspend the Counterparty's access to the Platform, API or Services for: (a) non-payment of undisputed Fees outstanding for more than [thirty (30)] days; (b) a security threat, breach or unauthorised access; (c) breach of the acceptable-use policy or usage limits; (d) legal, regulatory or compliance risk; or (e) the Counterparty's insolvency, sanctions designation or regulatory investigation. The Company shall give notice of suspension where operationally practicable.
45.fallback: Notice-and-Cure Before Suspension. For non-critical commercial breaches (other than security, regulatory, financial-crime or Customer-Asset matters), the Company shall give notice and a cure period not exceeding [five (5)] Business Days before suspending.
45.counselNotes: Notice-and-cure before suspension is acceptable only for non-critical commercial breaches; the Company must retain immediate suspension rights for security, regulatory, financial-crime, fraud and Customer-Asset risks.

46.title: Termination for Cause
46.buyside: Additional Company Termination Triggers. In addition to the Baseline, the Company may terminate immediately for: (a) chronic failure to meet Critical Service Levels in any [three (3)] consecutive months; (b) failure to maintain required insurance, licences or regulatory authorisations; (c) unauthorised subcontracting of regulated, data or security functions; (d) a change of control of the Counterparty to a Company competitor or sanctioned entity; or (e) any other event that, in the Company's reasonable judgement, creates material regulatory, security or operational risk.
46.sellside: Company Termination (Supplier). The Company may terminate this Agreement for cause on [thirty (30)] days' written notice for: (a) the Counterparty's persistent failure to pay undisputed amounts after demand; (b) the Counterparty's breach of the permitted-use or IP restrictions; or (c) any other material breach not remedied within the notice period.
46.counselNotes: A [thirty (30)]-day cure period is acceptable for non-critical, remediable commercial breaches; fraud, sanctions, data breach, regulatory breach, insolvency, misuse of Customer Assets and IP infringement must remain immediate-termination triggers with no cure.

47.title: Termination for Convenience
47.baseline: Termination for Convenience. The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving [30 / 60 / 90] days' written notice to the Counterparty. On such termination, the Company's sole obligation is to pay undisputed Fees for Services properly performed up to the termination date, and the Company shall not be liable for any other loss, cost or damage arising from a termination for convenience.
47.buyside: Buy-Side Convenience Rights. The Company shall have a termination-for-convenience right exercisable on [thirty (30)] days' notice for non-critical services, and [sixty (60)] days' notice for critical or operationally complex services, with no early-termination fee, break fee, minimum committed fees or wind-down costs unless expressly agreed and approved by Finance.
47.sellside: Convenience Rights (Company as Supplier). Where the Company is the supplier: (a) the Company may terminate for convenience on [thirty (30)] days' written notice; (b) the Counterparty may terminate for convenience on [ninety (90)] days' written notice; and (c) the Counterparty shall pay all Fees committed and properly invoiced up to the end of its notice period.
47.fallback: Mutual Convenience Termination (Non-Critical). For non-critical contracts, either Party may terminate for convenience on [sixty (60)] days' notice, provided that: (a) no early-termination fee applies; and (b) transition-assistance rights are preserved for the notice period.

48.title: Termination for Regulatory Reason
48.baseline: Termination for Regulatory Reason. The Company may terminate this Agreement immediately without liability if, in its reasonable opinion, continuation would or might: (a) breach Applicable Law or Regulatory Requirements applicable to the Company; (b) breach its licence conditions or a Regulator's expectations; (c) breach applicable sanctions, AML/CFT or financial-crime requirements; (d) compromise the Company's internal compliance standards; or (e) adversely affect the Company's regulatory standing, licence or product approvals. On such termination, the Company's obligations are limited to payment of undisputed Fees for Services properly performed up to the termination date.
48.buyside: Nature of the Regulatory Termination Right. The regulatory termination right shall be: (a) unilateral, not requiring the Counterparty's consent; (b) effective immediately on notice; (c) without penalty, break fee or liability; and (d) supported by transition assistance from the Counterparty for [ninety (90)] days after termination.
48.sellside: Regulatory Termination (Company as Supplier). Where the Company is the supplier, it may terminate or modify the Services immediately where: (a) a change in law, regulatory guidance or its licence conditions makes the Services impracticable or unlawful; or (b) the Counterparty's use of the Services creates legal or regulatory risk for the Company.
48.fallback: Notice-and-Consultation (Non-Imminent Risk). Where the regulatory risk is not imminent and does not require emergency action, the Company shall give notice and consult with the Counterparty before terminating for regulatory reason.
48.counselNotes: Use notice-and-consultation only where the regulatory risk is not imminent; retain the immediate regulatory termination right for urgent or emergency situations.

49.title: Termination for Security Incident or Data Breach
49.baseline: Termination for Security Incident or Data Breach. The Company may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if: (a) a Security Incident or breach of Personal Data materially affects the Company, its End Users, Personal Data, Customer Assets, systems or regulated operations; or (b) the Counterparty fails to notify the Company in accordance with Clause [●] (Security Incident and Data Breach Notification), or fails to remediate a Security Incident to the Company's reasonable satisfaction within [thirty (30)] days. The Counterparty shall cooperate fully with forensic investigation and regulatory notification following termination.
49.buyside: Investigation and Evidence Preservation. The Company may suspend access and initiate a forensic investigation before deciding whether to terminate. The Counterparty shall: (a) not delete, alter or destroy any evidence relating to the Security Incident without the Company's written consent; (b) cooperate with the Company's appointed forensic investigators; and (c) bear all costs of investigation, notification and remediation attributable to its systems or conduct.
49.sellside: Security Suspension or Termination (Company as Supplier). The Company may terminate or suspend the Counterparty's access immediately if the Counterparty's systems, personnel or integrations create a security threat to the Company's Platform or Customer Assets, including unauthorised access attempts, credential compromise or suspicious transaction patterns.
49.fallback: Cure Period (Minor Incidents). A [thirty (30)]-day cure period applies to minor security incidents that do not affect customer data, Customer Assets or regulated systems, and do not require regulatory notification.
49.counselNotes: A cure period is acceptable only for minor incidents with no customer-data, Customer-Asset, regulated-system or regulatory-notification impact; otherwise the immediate termination right applies.

50.title: Termination for Insolvency, Change of Control, Sanctions, Illegality or Reputational Risk
50.buyside: Change-of-Control Notification. In addition: (a) the Counterparty shall notify the Company immediately of any proposed Change of Control; (b) the Company shall have [thirty (30)] days from receipt of that notice to exercise its termination right; (c) the notice shall include full details of the acquirer, the acquiring entity, the ownership structure and its regulatory status; and (d) the Counterparty shall bear all transition costs where termination is triggered by a Change of Control.
50.sellside: Insolvency/Sanctions Termination (Company as Supplier). The Company may terminate for the Counterparty's insolvency or sanctions designation without liability, and the Counterparty shall have no claim against the Company for loss of anticipated profits, sunk costs or break fees following such termination.
50.fallback: Mutual Insolvency Termination. Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately if the other becomes insolvent, is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, or enters any analogous insolvency process.
50.counselNotes: Accept mutual insolvency termination rights. Resist any broad, subjective reputational-risk termination against the Company unless it is mutual, objective (tied to specified triggers) and subject to a notice-and-cure period.

51.title: Consequences of Termination
51.baseline: Consequences of Termination. Termination or expiry of this Agreement shall not affect: (a) any accrued rights or liabilities of either Party; (b) any Clause expressed to survive termination or expiry; or (c) any obligation that by its nature is intended to survive. On termination or expiry: (d) each Party shall immediately cease using the other's Confidential Information, Intellectual Property Rights and materials; (e) the Counterparty shall cease providing the Services except as required for transition; (f) the Counterparty shall return, transfer or securely delete all of the Company's Confidential Information, Personal Data and Customer Assets as directed by the Company; and (g) any outstanding undisputed Fees for Services properly performed shall be paid.
51.buyside: Counterparty Exit Obligations. On termination or expiry, the Counterparty shall, within [thirty (30)] days: (a) return all of the Company's Confidential Information and Personal Data in an agreed format; (b) provide written confirmation of secure deletion where requested; (c) deliver all work in progress, Deliverables, code, data and documentation; (d) transfer all licences, third-party contracts and operational arrangements necessary for the continuity of the Company's operations as directed; and (e) cooperate fully with transition to the Company's replacement provider.
51.sellside: Counterparty Wind-Down (Company as Supplier). On termination or expiry of the Counterparty's access rights, the Counterparty shall: (a) immediately cease all use of the Company's Platform, APIs and Confidential Information; (b) delete all Company materials from its systems and provide written confirmation; and (c) pay all outstanding undisputed Fees.
51.fallback: Extended Transition Period. For a complex operational handover, a transition period of up to [sixty (60)] days applies, provided the Counterparty continues the Services at the current Service Levels throughout the transition.

52.title: Exit Assistance, Transition, Migration and Data Return
52.baseline: Exit Assistance, Transition, Migration and Data Return. On the Company's request at any time during the Term or following termination or expiry, the Counterparty shall provide exit assistance and transition support for up to [6 / 12] months, including: (a) migration of the Company's data in agreed formats to the Company or its designated replacement provider; (b) knowledge transfer and documentation of all systems, configurations, processes and integrations; (c) operational support at agreed rates; and (d) continuation of the Services at the current Service Levels during the transition, in each case without degradation of the Services or any proprietary restriction on data access.
52.buyside: Enhanced Exit Assistance. Exit assistance shall be: (a) mandatory for all critical services and services involving Customer Assets, Personal Data or regulated functions; (b) provided within [thirty (30)] days of the Company's written transition request; (c) at commercially reasonable rates agreed in advance; and (d) free of charge for the first [thirty (30)] days following a termination for the Counterparty's cause.
52.sellside: Company Migration Support. The Company will provide the Counterparty with standard data-export functionality and migration support as part of the Services at the end of the Term, subject to applicable technical, security and legal limitations. Extended or bespoke migration support is available at the Company's published professional-services rates.
52.counselNotes: Paid exit assistance for ordinary services is acceptable provided that: (a) the Counterparty cannot impose proprietary lock-in or block data access during transition; and (b) the rates for exit assistance are pre-agreed in the contract.

53.title: Force Majeure
53.baseline: Force Majeure. No Party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent caused by a Force Majeure Event beyond its reasonable control, provided that: (a) the affected Party gives written notice to the other promptly and no later than [five (5)] Business Days after the Force Majeure Event arises, specifying its nature and expected duration; (b) the affected Party takes all reasonable steps to mitigate the impact and resume performance as soon as practicable; and (c) the affected Party continues to perform all obligations not affected by the Force Majeure Event. Force majeure shall not excuse: (d) payment obligations accrued before the Force Majeure Event; (e) confidentiality, data-protection, information-security, Customer-Asset safeguarding or regulatory-cooperation obligations; or (f) obligations where the Force Majeure Event was foreseeable and preventable by the affected Party.
53.buyside: Force Majeure (Critical Services). For critical services: (a) the Counterparty's force-majeure relief is excluded to the extent the event was caused or contributed to by its inadequate security controls, single points of failure or inadequate business continuity; (b) if a Force Majeure Event continues for more than [thirty (30)] days, the Company may terminate immediately without liability; and (c) data, Customer-Asset safeguarding and regulatory obligations continue regardless of force majeure.
53.sellside: Third-Party Infrastructure. The Company is not responsible for force-majeure events affecting third-party infrastructure, blockchain networks, exchange platforms, payment networks, settlement systems or cloud service providers. The Counterparty accepts these risks where the Services depend on third-party infrastructure outside the Company's control.
53.fallback: Mutual Force Majeure. Either Party may claim force-majeure relief, subject to: (a) a notice requirement of not less than [five (5)] Business Days; (b) an obligation to mitigate; and (c) a right for either Party to terminate if the event continues for more than [30 / 60] days.

54.title: Material Adverse Change
54.baseline: Material Adverse Change. The Company may suspend or terminate this Agreement by written notice if a material adverse change occurs in the Counterparty's: (a) financial condition, solvency or creditworthiness; (b) regulatory status, licence standing or relationship with any Regulator; (c) security posture, including a material increase in security risk or repeated security incidents; (d) beneficial ownership or control structure; or (e) ability to perform its material obligations under this Agreement, and that change is not remedied within [thirty (30)] days of the Company's written notice.
54.buyside: Financial Covenants. For long-term, critical or strategic contracts, the Counterparty shall maintain the minimum financial ratios or metrics specified in Schedule [●] and shall notify the Company immediately of any event that triggers, or is likely to trigger, a material adverse change.
54.sellside: MAC Against the Company. The Company does not accept any broad or subjective material-adverse-change termination right against it. Any such right against the Company must be: (a) objective and limited to specified defined events; and (b) subject to a [thirty (30)]-day notice and cure period.
54.fallback: MAC (Limited Triggers). For shorter-term or lower-risk contracts, the material-adverse-change right is limited to insolvency, sanctions and loss of a regulatory licence.
54.counselNotes: For shorter-term or lower-risk contracts, limit MAC triggers to insolvency, sanctions and regulatory-licence loss; reserve the broader triggers for long-term, critical or strategic contracts.

55.title: Change in Law
55.baseline: Change in Law. If a change in Applicable Law or Regulatory Requirements after the Effective Date materially affects a Party's ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement, the Parties shall promptly discuss and agree the necessary amendments. The Company may terminate this Agreement without liability, penalty or break fee where: (a) continuation would be unlawful or contrary to Regulatory Requirements applicable to the Company; (b) continuation would be commercially impracticable for the Company; or (c) the required amendments cannot be agreed within [sixty (60)] days.
55.buyside: Counterparty's Compliance Costs. The cost of complying with changes in law applicable to the Counterparty's business, personnel, systems or services shall be borne by the Counterparty. The Company shall not bear compliance costs for obligations that apply to the Counterparty as a matter of law.
55.sellside: Company Cost Pass-Through. Where a change in law materially and demonstrably increases the Company's cost of providing the Services, the Company may: (a) notify the Counterparty of the impact and a proposed fee adjustment; and (b) if the Counterparty does not agree to the adjustment within [thirty (30)] days, terminate on [sixty (60)] days' notice.
55.fallback: Equitable Cost Adjustment. Where a change in law imposes materially new and verifiable obligations on both Parties, the Parties shall agree an equitable adjustment to the Fees, with the scope and cost agreed and documented.

56.title: Assignment, Novation, Transfer and Change of Control
56.baseline: Assignment, Novation, Transfer and Change of Control. Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, sub-licence or otherwise deal with its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, except that the Company may assign or transfer its rights and obligations to: (a) a Company Affiliate; (b) a successor entity following a merger, reorganisation or transfer of all or substantially all of the Company's business to which this Agreement relates; or (c) as required in connection with financing, securitisation or group restructuring. Any purported assignment in breach of this Clause is void.
56.buyside: Assignment Controls. In addition: (a) the Counterparty shall not assign or transfer to a Company competitor, a sanctioned entity, or an entity that creates legal, regulatory or reputational risk for the Company; (b) a Change of Control of the Counterparty shall be treated as an assignment requiring the Company's consent; and (c) the Company may withhold consent to any assignment where it determines, in its reasonable judgement, that the proposed assignee does not meet its due-diligence, regulatory or security standards.
56.sellside: Company Assignment Freedom. The Company may assign or transfer its rights and obligations to any Company entity or any successor as part of a group reorganisation without consent. The Counterparty shall not assign, transfer, novate or subcontract its obligations without the Company's prior written consent.
56.counselNotes: Permit assignment to existing Company Affiliates or intra-group restructuring without consent. The Counterparty may be permitted to assign to a non-competitor that demonstrates equivalent capability and creditworthiness, subject to the Company's right to conduct due diligence.

57.title: Relationship of Parties; No Partnership, Agency or Fiduciary Duty
57.baseline: Relationship of the Parties. The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates, or is intended to create, a partnership, joint venture, employment relationship, agency, trust, fiduciary relationship or association, or any authority for either Party to bind, represent or act on behalf of the other, unless expressly stated.
57.buyside: No Counterparty Authority. The Counterparty has no authority to: (a) make any representation, warranty or commitment on behalf of the Company; (b) bind the Company to any contract, obligation or communication; (c) hold itself out as the Company's agent, representative, distributor or partner without the Company's written consent; or (d) conduct any regulated activity on behalf of the Company or through the Company's licence.
57.sellside: No Company Advisory or Fiduciary Role. The Company does not provide investment advice, financial planning, tax advice, custodial services, brokerage, dealing, trust services, fiduciary services or any other regulated or advisory service to the Counterparty through this Agreement, unless expressly and separately agreed and licensed.
57.counselNotes: For referral, marketing and introducer arrangements, add express limitations on the Counterparty's authority to make regulated statements, financial promotions or product claims on behalf of the Company.

58.title: Notices
58.baseline: Notices. Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by: (a) hand delivery; (b) reputable overnight courier; (c) registered or certified mail; or (d) email to the address specified in this Agreement, with read receipt or delivery confirmation. Notices are effective on confirmed delivery or, for email, on receipt of a delivery confirmation or read receipt from the intended recipient. Each Party shall maintain up-to-date notice addresses and promptly notify the other of any change.
58.buyside: Copies to Legal. All formal notices (including breach notices, termination notices, claims and regulatory notices) shall be copied to: (a) the Company's Legal team at [legal@company-domain] (or as updated by the Company); and (b) the Counterparty's General Counsel or Legal department at [address]. A notice sent to business contacts only, without a copy to Legal, shall not be effective for formal breach, termination or claim purposes.
58.sellside: Operational Notices. The Company may give operational notices (including SLA reports, invoices, product updates and non-material communications) by email to the Counterparty's designated operational contact. Formal breach, termination, indemnity and regulatory notices require the formal notice procedure above.
58.counselNotes: Email is acceptable for ordinary communications, but require a copy to Legal for any notice of breach, termination, claim or regulatory matter.

59.title: Entire Agreement
59.baseline: Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, proposals, negotiations, representations, warranties and communications, whether oral or written, relating to that subject matter. Each Party acknowledges that it has not relied on any representation, warranty or statement not expressly set out in this Agreement in entering into it; this Clause does not limit or exclude liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.
59.buyside: Non-Reliance (Company). The Company has not relied on any product claim, technology-performance guarantee, regulatory assurance, feasibility statement, reference implementation or marketing material provided by the Counterparty that is not expressly included in this Agreement. Any such representation must be documented in a Schedule or warranty in this Agreement before signature.
59.sellside: Non-Reliance (Counterparty). The Counterparty has not relied on any representation by the Company as to anticipated usage volumes, revenue projections, customer acquisition, market performance or business outcomes that is not expressly stated in this Agreement.
59.counselNotes: A standard entire-agreement clause is acceptable provided that: (a) the fraud carve-out is preserved; and (b) all agreed business terms are documented in the contract before signature.

60.title: Amendments and Variations
60.baseline: Amendments and Variations. No amendment, modification, variation, waiver or supplement to this Agreement is valid or binding unless made in writing and signed by an authorised representative of each Party. No act, omission, conduct or course of dealing shall constitute an amendment or waiver unless documented in accordance with this Clause.
60.buyside: Amendment Controls. Amendments affecting price, scope, the Service Levels, liability, data flows, security architecture, regulatory obligations, subcontracting or any other material term require: (a) the Company's Legal review and sign-off; and (b) signature by a signatory with authority under the Company's delegation of authority. The Company does not accept "click-to-accept", or continued use of the Services, as a mechanism for amending negotiated contractual terms.
60.sellside: Company Policy Amendments. The Company may amend its acceptable-use policy, security requirements and platform policies on [thirty (30)] days' notice. Amendments to negotiated core terms (pricing, liability, IP, data, termination) require mutual written agreement.
60.counselNotes: Operational change orders are acceptable provided they are signed by authorised representatives and do not affect legal, regulatory, security, liability or pricing terms.

61.title: Waiver
61.baseline: Waiver. No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right, power or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver of it, and no single or partial exercise of any right, power or remedy precludes any other or further exercise of that or any other right. A waiver of any breach does not waive any subsequent breach. A waiver is effective only if made in writing and signed by an authorised representative of the waiving Party, and applies only to the specific circumstances and instance expressly stated.
61.counselNotes: Remedies are cumulative; ensure a waiver cannot be implied from course of dealing, forbearance, delay, acceptance of payment or partial enforcement. The Company's acceptance of payment, continued provision of the Services or forbearance from enforcement does not waive any right.

62.title: Severability
62.baseline: Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable by any court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, that provision shall be (a) modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal and enforceable; or (b) deleted if modification is not possible, and the remainder of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect. The Parties shall use reasonable efforts to agree a replacement provision that achieves, as closely as possible, the original commercial intent and effect of the deleted provision.
62.counselNotes: Where available under applicable law, include a "blue pencil" qualifier allowing a court to modify rather than delete a non-compliant provision (particularly for restraint-of-trade and non-compete clauses).

63.title: Further Assurance
63.baseline: Further Assurance. Each Party shall promptly execute and deliver all documents, and take all actions, reasonably necessary or desirable to give full effect to this Agreement and the transactions contemplated by it.
63.buyside: Enhanced Further Assurance. For IP assignments, regulatory filings, data migrations, security transitions and asset transfers, the Counterparty shall complete the required acts within the timeline specified by the Company, and the Company may execute documents on the Counterparty's behalf as its attorney-in-fact if the Counterparty fails to act within [ten (10)] Business Days of request.
63.sellside: Company Further Assurance (Limited). The Company's further-assurance obligations are limited to acts within its reasonable control and shall not require it to incur material costs, make regulatory filings on the Counterparty's behalf, or take any action inconsistent with its regulatory or legal obligations.
63.counselNotes: For low-risk contracts, a standard further-assurance obligation bounded by reasonable acts within each Party's control is acceptable.

64.title: Cumulative Remedies
64.baseline: Cumulative Remedies. The rights and remedies under this Agreement are cumulative and are not exclusive of any other rights or remedies provided by law, in equity or otherwise, unless this Agreement expressly states that a specified remedy is the sole remedy for a specified breach.
64.buyside: Company Remedies. The Company is not limited to its contractual remedies; all equitable, legal, statutory and contractual remedies are available for breach of this Agreement.
